deck.title: KMS & CloudHSM
deck.analogy: KMS is the bank's shared vault with a signing register (CloudTrail); CloudHSM is renting your own private vault room that even the bank staff cannot see inside.

subtopics.title: CloudHSM — when the shared vault isn't enough

cards.front: What is the hard part of encryption, and what does AWS KMS do about it?

back.answer: The hard part is key management; KMS stores and manages encryption keys centrally and integrates with nearly every AWS service.
back.explanation: KMS is the shared vault: AWS runs it and every key use is logged in CloudTrail.
back.mnemonic: KMS = bank's shared vault with a signing register (CloudTrail).

cards.front: What is KMS's superpower for auditing?

back.answer: Every key use is logged in CloudTrail, giving a full audit trail.
back.explanation: The register in the vault analogy is CloudTrail.
back.mnemonic: Every key use is written in the register.

cards.front: What is CloudHSM compared to KMS in the vault analogy, and what does HSM stand for?

back.answer: CloudHSM is your own private vault room: dedicated hardware where even AWS can't see inside. HSM = Hardware Security Module.
back.explanation: An HSM is a tamper-resistant physical device performing crypto operations.
back.mnemonic: CloudHSM = renting an entire private vault room.

cards.front: KMS AWS-managed keys (aws/s3 etc.): cost, rotation, control?

back.answer: Free, automatic rotation, no control — AWS runs it.

cards.front: KMS customer-managed key (CMK): cost, rotation, control?

back.answer: $1/month, optional yearly auto-rotation, full control (key policy, disable/delete).
back.explanation: Choose it for own key policy, cross-account grants, or auditable rotation.

cards.front: What are KMS AWS-owned keys?

back.answer: Invisible keys shared across accounts; you never see them and have no control.

cards.front: KMS: which key type when you need your own key policy, cross-account grants, and auditable rotation?

back.explanation: AWS-managed and AWS-owned keys give you no control.

cards.front: A user has kms:* in IAM but gets AccessDenied on a KMS key. Why?

back.answer: The key policy doesn't allow them; both the key policy and IAM policy must allow.
back.explanation: IAM permission alone is not enough for KMS key use.

cards.front: What is the maximum data size KMS can directly encrypt?

back.explanation: Larger data requires envelope encryption via GenerateDataKey.

cards.front: How does KMS envelope encryption with GenerateDataKey work?

back.answer: KMS returns a plaintext data key and an encrypted data key; encrypt locally, discard plaintext key, store encrypted key with the ciphertext.
back.explanation: To decrypt, send the encrypted data key to KMS to unwrap, then decrypt locally. Big data never goes to KMS.
back.code:
GenerateDataKey -> KMS returns:
  plaintext data key (encrypt locally, then discard)
  encrypted data key (store with ciphertext)
Decrypt: encrypted data key -> KMS unwraps -> decrypt locally

cards.front: KMS: "Encrypt a large file with KMS" — is "KMS encrypts it directly" correct?

back.explanation: KMS only wraps/unwraps the small data key.

cards.front: Can a KMS key be deleted immediately?

back.answer: No — scheduled deletion has a mandatory 7–30 day waiting period (default 30).
back.explanation: Deleting makes everything it encrypted unrecoverable. To stop use right now, disable the key (instant, reversible).

cards.front: What is the default KMS key deletion waiting period?
What are KMS multi-Region keys and their use cases?

back.answer: Same key material replicated across Regions with matching key IDs: encrypt in one Region, decrypt in another.
back.explanation: Use cases: DynamoDB global tables, cross-Region DR, client-side encryption of globally moving data.

cards.front: What does an S3 Bucket Key do with SSE-KMS, and what is the trade-off?

back.answer: Uses a short-lived bucket-level key, so far fewer KMS calls (~99% cheaper requests), but coarser CloudTrail audit granularity.
back.explanation: You see bucket-key events, not one event per object.

cards.front: CloudHSM vs KMS: FIPS 140-2 validation levels?

back.answer: CloudHSM is Level 3; KMS is Level 2.
back.explanation: Level 3 adds physical tamper-resistance requirements. "Level 3" in a question means CloudHSM.

cards.front: What is CloudHSM and who manages the keys?

back.answer: Dedicated, single-tenant HSMs in your VPC; you manage the keys, AWS has no access (AWS manages hardware only).

cards.sourceHeading: CloudHSM — when the shared vault isn't enough

cards.front: What are CloudHSM use cases?

back.answer: Strict regulatory/compliance mandates, BYOK-style full key custody, SSL/TLS offload, running your own CA.

cards.sourceHeading: CloudHSM — when the shared vault isn't enough

cards.front: KMS vs CloudHSM decision rule?

back.answer: "AWS can't access keys", FIPS Level 3, dedicated hardware → CloudHSM; integration, audit, low cost, ease → KMS.

cards.sourceHeading: CloudHSM — when the shared vault isn't enough

cards.front: Security team must audit every use of an encryption key. Which AWS solution?

choices.why: Every KMS key use is logged in CloudTrail.

cards.front: You must encrypt a 100MB file using KMS. What approach?

choices.why: Data key encrypts locally; KMS wraps it.

cards.front: A compromised KMS key must be deleted immediately. What is the answer?

back.answer: Impossible — 7–30 day mandatory wait; disable it now instead.

choices.text: Delete it immediately via the API

choices.why: Doesn't stop use of the compromised key.

choices.text: Impossible immediately; disable it, schedule deletion
choices.why: Disable is instant; deletion waits 7–30 days.

cards.front: Compliance requires FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated modules. Which service?
Keys must be inaccessible even to AWS. Which service?

choices.why: You manage keys; AWS has no access.

cards.front: Encrypt data in us-east-1 and decrypt the same ciphertext in eu-west-1 (DR/global tables). Which feature?
Keys must rotate automatically every year under company control. Which option?
KMS request costs exploded from millions of S3 objects using SSE-KMS. Fix?

back.answer: Enable S3 Bucket Key (accept coarser audit).

cards.front: User has full IAM KMS permissions but gets AccessDenied on a key. Cause?

back.answer: Key policy doesn't allow them; both key policy and IAM must permit.

choices.why: Both key policy and IAM must allow.
